summary: Tucked into a narrow creek valley where the western slopes of Mount Tamalpais funnel down into the flatlands of central Marin County, San Anselmo packs a surprising amount of small-town density — 4,637 people per square mile — into just 2.7 square miles, giving it the compressed, walkable feel of a village that never sprawled. The commercial spine along San Anselmo Avenue hosts independent coffee shops, antique stores, and sit-down restaurants that would be unremarkable in a bigger city but feel improbably concentrated for a town of 12,500. San Anselmo Creek runs right through the center of town, and open-space preserves climb the surrounding ridgelines, so a casual after-work hike into oak-studded hillsides is measured in minutes, not miles. Average daily highs hover around 67°F with nine hours of sunshine, though the inland valley position means summer afternoons run warmer than the foggy coast just a few miles west. The affordability math is stark: a median home price of $1,524,300 against a median household income of $170,457 yields a price-to-income ratio near 9:1, and even renting at $2,750 a month claims nearly 20% of that median gross income. With almost no major employers within town limits, this is fundamentally a bedroom community — most working residents commute south toward San Francisco or east toward the broader Bay Area, typically via Highway 101. San Anselmo delivers a rare geographic intimacy between ridgeline wilderness and a genuine downtown, but the cost of that proximity is embedded in every mortgage payment.
